nodes.summary: `π(s)` solves Haldane's equation `1 - π = exp (-(1 + s) π)`.
nodes.title: Haldane's equation for the survival probability

nodes.summary: The Poisson(`r`) generating function: `∑ e^{-r} r^k / k! x^k = exp (r (x - 1))`.
nodes.title: Generating function of the Poisson distribution

nodes.summary: The survival probability is less than `1`: the mutant leaves no copies with positive probability `exp (-(1 + s))`. (For `s < -1`, outside the model, `π(s) = 0`.)
nodes.title: Survival probability is less than one

nodes.summary: A beneficial mutant survives with positive probability.
nodes.title: Beneficial mutant survives with positive probability

nodes.summary: Haldane's survival probability `π(s) = 1 - q(s)` of a mutant with selective advantage `s` per generation, whose number of copies in the next generation is Poisson with mean `1 + s`. The model needs `s ≥ -1`; for `s < -1` the mean is truncated to `0` (`Real.toNNReal`), the mutant leaves no copies, and `π(s) = 0`.
nodes.title: Haldane's survival probability of a mutant
